learningObjectives: Locate the File Operations and Folder Operations Modules in the Standard subset.
Create, read, append to, copy, move, rename, and delete files from a TestCase.
Verify file and folder existence, and compare file contents.
Recognise which Modules require a pre-existing target directory and which create one.
Avoid the common traps — notably that TBox Delete File reports success even when the file was never there.
Tell apart Excel UI Engine 3.0, Excel Engine 3.0, Database Engine 3.0, HTML modules, and TBox Evaluation Tool by the action each one performs.
Locate current XML Modules under Engines → XML and distinguish resource operations.
Match Windows/Buffer/Process Operations Modules (Start Program, Name To Buffer, Partial Buffer, Clipboard) to their purpose.
Distinguish standard Windows dialogs, custom dialogs and JavaScript dialogs before selecting a Module.
Explain JSON object/array identification, editable TestStepValue names and independently configured repetition.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Why file automation belongs in a test

elements.description: Most non-trivial TestCases touch the file system somewhere. A test needs an input file placed in a watched folder before it starts; an export must be verified after it runs; yesterday's output has to be cleared so today's run is clean; a generated report needs archiving as evidence. Doing any of that by hand defeats the point of automation, and the Standard subset provides Modules for all of it — no scanning and no engine-specific work required.

elements.text: These Modules live under TBox Automation Tools in the Standard subset, split across two folders: File Operations and Folder Operations.

elements.title: Examples of File Operations Modules
items: TBox Read/Create File
TBox Append File
TBox Copy File
TBox Move/Rename File
TBox Delete File
TBox File Existence
TBox File Compare
TBox Image Compare

elements.title: Related Standard subset groups (not an exhaustive course inventory)
items: Basic Windows Operations — Clipboard, Dialog and Context Menu handling.
Buffer Operations — Set Buffer, Name To Buffer, Partial Buffer and Delete Buffer; current versions also include array operations.
Process Operations — Start Program and Close Program.
Expression Evaluation — TBox Evaluation Tool.
Other Module groups depend on the installed subset/version; inspect the current catalogue rather than assuming a legacy course inventory.

bulletPoints: Standard subset → TBox Automation Tools → File Operations / Folder Operations.
Nothing to scan — these Modules are ready to use straight from the Standard subset.

elements.title: The four folder Modules
items: TBox Create Folder — creates a folder in a specific location.
TBox Copy Folder — copies a folder to a specific location.
TBox Delete Folder — deletes a directory.
TBox Folder Existence — verifies whether a folder exists in a specific directory.

elements.text: File Copy and Move require an existing target directory. Do not transfer that rule to every folder Module: Copy Folder can create a missing target, and Delete Folder only deletes empty folders unless Recursive is True.

bulletPoints: Create · Copy · Delete · Existence — the folder-level toolkit.

elements.description: The dual-purpose workhorse: it creates files and writes text content, and it also verifies or buffers text content from an existing file. Encoding is configurable — UTF-8, UTF-16 and ISO-8859-1 are supported, with an optional byte order mark setting. Buffering content out of a file is how you feed data read from disk into later TestSteps.
Append File adds text and creates the file if absent. Optional encoding and newline settings apply; this does not guarantee that an invalid path, permissions or conflicting file lock can be ignored.

bulletPoints: Read/Create File writes AND verifies/buffers — one Module, both directions.
Append File auto-creates the file when it is missing.

elements.description: Duplicates a file into another directory. The target directory must already exist at run time — this Module will not create it for you, which is why a TBox Create Folder step often precedes it. Tricentis also notes the Module might not work if a security and password management tool is in play.
Relocates a file, renames it, or both. As with Copy File, the target directory must pre-exist for a move to succeed.
Delete File returns a positive result when no matching file is found. This permits missing-file cleanup but does not prove prior existence or guarantee success for permission, lock or path errors.

elements.text: A positive missing-file delete result is not an export assertion. Check existence first when required, and still investigate real filesystem errors.

bulletPoints: Copy File and Move/Rename File both require the target directory to exist beforehand.
A missing file produces a positive delete result; other failures are not thereby excluded.

elements.description: Verifies whether a file exists in a directory. It supports negation with '!' (assert a file is absent), wildcards with '*' (match a pattern rather than an exact name), and the WaitOn ActionMode — which is what you use when a file is produced asynchronously and the test must wait for it to appear rather than checking once and failing.

Compares the content of two files and can optionally generate a diff report. Where the second file has additional content, the Module highlights that in green in the report — useful when the question is not merely 'are these identical?' but 'what changed?'.

Verifies image files (BMP, JPG, GIF) with a pixel-accurate comparison — an exact pixel match, not a similarity threshold. Note the contrast with PDF 1:1 Compare from Lesson 2, which passes when similarity exceeds an accuracy you specify. Image Compare is the stricter of the two.

elements.text: The current File Operations reference includes Zip File and Unzip File. In the supplied original AE1 base subset, its File Operations folder contains eight Modules: Image Compare, File Existence, File Compare, Delete File, Copy File, Read/Create File, Append File and Move/Rename File (all TBox). Zip/Unzip are not in that folder. This is a static package inventory, not proof of installed-version availability or runtime behavior.
📄 Official Tricentis Academy exercise material for this lesson is not redistributed here — complete the exercises inside the official course.

bulletPoints: File Existence: '!' negates, '*' wildcards, WaitOn waits for asynchronous output.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Matching actions to Engines: Excel, Database, Browser, and Expressions

elements.description: Steers the MS Excel application itself — driving it the way a user would, through its own interface. Use it when the TestCase needs to interact with Excel as an application, not just its data.

Excel Engine works with workbook content without driving the visible Excel UI. Choose it for content operations; installed prerequisites still apply and it is not universally faster or more stable than UI steering.
Database Engine executes database operations through SQL statements. Use its compatible open/operate/close Modules or DB Expert; confirm the supported connection and driver.

Cover browser and document-level actions that sit above individual HTML controls — such as Execute JavaScript, Open a URL, and Close Browser. These act on the browser session itself, not on a specific button or field inside the page.

TBox Evaluation Tool verifies expressions that resolve to TRUE or FALSE. Use ActionMode Verify, quote values intended as strings, and account for supported dynamic expressions and NCalc special-character escaping. A string representation of a date is not automatically a chronological date comparison.

elements.text: The naming convention is the tell: 'Excel UI Engine' drives the application's interface, plain 'Excel Engine' drives the file directly. The same UI-vs-file distinction shows up across other Engines too.

bulletPoints: Excel UI Engine 3.0 → the Excel application. Excel Engine 3.0 → Excel files directly.
Database Engine 3.0 → query/steer database data sets.
HTML modules → browser/document-level actions (JavaScript, URL, Close Browser).
TBox Evaluation Tool → compares numeric/string/alphanumeric expressions.

elements.text: Current location: Standard modules → Engines → XML. The four operations below are examples; the folder also includes validation, signing and XPath evaluation Modules.

elements.title: Four resource/file operations
items: Open/Create XML file — create a new XML file, or load an existing file as a Resource.
Create XML Resource — creates an empty XML resource, with no file needed yet.
Save XML file — transfers the modifications made to the resource to the connected XML file.
Verify XML — verifies XML resource content by using DotNet XPath expressions.

elements.description: An XML Resource is Tosca's in-memory working copy — Create XML Resource makes one without any file on disk. Open/Create XML file can either make a brand-new file or load an existing one as a Resource. Save XML file is the step that commits an in-memory Resource's changes back to disk.

bulletPoints: Engines → XML includes Open/Create XML file, Create XML Resource, Save XML file and Verify XML; this is not an exhaustive catalogue.
Verify XML uses DotNet XPath expressions to check resource content.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Bonus: the JSON Engine — reading a repeating array with one TestCase

elements.description: Current JSON Module guidance uses XScan. JSON object members are identified by name and treated as unordered pairs; array entries are positional and named item#<position>. Verify the generated structure and data types rather than assuming every export workflow is identical.
The Configuration Param ExplicitName=True permits editing the referenced XTestStepValue name. It does not itself activate wildcard matching or prove that a chosen name selects every JSON array entry.

elements.term: Counts and repetition are separate concerns
elements.description: ResultCount describes occurrences of the current node. TestStepFolder Repetition accepts a non-negative integer or dynamic expression, and {REPETITION} identifies the current pass. For variable-length JSON, validate counting and position selection against the actual Module; repetition alone does not guarantee coverage of each array element.

elements.text: The original 2022 Academy exercise was inspected in full. It uses an API Scan XML/JSON export and an item* ModuleAttribute template, then explicitly counts and indexes the matching nodes. This source prescription is distinct from current XScan guidance and does not prove successful execution for empty, single-entry or changed-schema inputs.

items: In the original Ratings.json exercise, export an XML/JSON TestCase from API Scan. Keep the first array-entry template, name its ModuleAttribute item* and set ExplicitName=True for editable TestStepValue names.
Open the file as resource Ratings. Use the source Buffer expression .ResultCount == ratingsCount on the matching node to capture its count.
Set the repeating folder property to {B[ratingsCount]}. In its reading step, use #{REPETITION} as the entry name and buffer each field under a name containing {REPETITION}.
Run the training TestCase and compare captured count and indexed field values with the input. Test boundary cases independently before reusing this recipe.

bulletPoints: Object members: name-based; array elements: position-based.
ExplicitName changes whether the TestStepValue name is editable, not whether an array is fully traversed.
Count, index selection and repetition are separate parts of the inspected source recipe; validate them against actual inputs.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Windows, Buffer, and Process Operations — matching actions to Modules

elements.description: TBox Dialog handles standard Microsoft Windows dialogs without scanning. Customized dialogs must be scanned first. Caption identifies the dialog window, optional Label further narrows it using message text, and Button supplies the text of the button to confirm. JavaScript dialogs have a separate HTML Module, Steer Dialog Box.

elements.text: Use the actual dialog and button text in the applicable Module. Do not infer that every confirmation popup is an unscanned Windows dialog or that changing letter case is the guaranteed fix for any failed click.

rows: Open an application or an executable file
Buffer the name of the TestCase that uses the Module
Verify or buffer only part of a value
Copy text to the Windows clipboard, or verify/buffer text from it
Verify existence, or create/copy/delete a folder
Folder Operations Modules (TBox Create Folder, Copy Folder, Delete Folder, Folder Existence)

elements.text: Set Buffer creates or verifies a supplied value. Name To Buffer captures the TestCase name during ExecutionList execution; ScratchBook does not support it. Partial Buffer extracts or verifies a selected part of a value.

bulletPoints: TBox Start Program opens applications/executables.
Name To Buffer = the TestCase's own name; Partial Buffer = part of a value; Set Buffer = a value you supply.
TBox Clipboard reads/writes the Windows clipboard.
Folder existence/create/copy/delete all live under the Folder Operations Modules group.

examPitfalls.title: Treating a passing TBox Delete File as proof the file existed
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Deleting an expected export file and taking the green result as confirmation that the export ran.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: TBox Delete File returns a positive result even if the file does not exist. Verify with TBox File Existence first if the file's presence is what you actually need to assert.

examPitfalls.title: Copying or moving into a directory that doesn't exist yet
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Using TBox Copy File or TBox Move/Rename File with a target path whose folder has not been created.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Both require the target directory to exist at run time. Precede them with TBox Create Folder.

examPitfalls.title: Checking once for a file that is produced asynchronously
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Running TBox File Existence immediately after triggering an export and failing because the file has not been written yet.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: TBox File Existence supports the WaitOn ActionMode. Use it so the TestCase waits for the file to appear rather than making a single check at the wrong moment.

examPitfalls.title: Expecting TBox Image Compare to tolerate small differences
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Using Image Compare on a screenshot that varies slightly between runs and expecting a similarity threshold to absorb it.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: TBox Image Compare is pixel-accurate — an exact match. It is not the same as PDF 1:1 Compare, which passes when similarity exceeds a configurable accuracy.

examPitfalls.title: Adding a create step before every Append
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Pairing TBox Read/Create File with TBox Append File just to guarantee the target file exists.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: TBox Append File creates the file automatically if it is not there. The extra create step is unnecessary.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming Excel Engine and Excel UI Engine are interchangeable
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Picking Excel Engine 3.0 for a step that actually needs to click around inside the live Excel application, or vice versa.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Excel Engine 3.0 steers Excel files directly. Excel UI Engine 3.0 drives the Excel application's own interface. Choose based on whether you need the file's data or the application's UI.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing TBox Name To Buffer with TBox Set Buffer or TBox Partial Buffer
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Reaching for the wrong Buffer Operations Module when the goal is simply to capture the current TestCase's name, or to extract only part of a value.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: TBox Set Buffer stores a value you supply. TBox Name To Buffer automatically stores the current TestCase's own name. TBox Partial Buffer extracts or verifies only part of a larger value. Pick based on where the value should come from. Name To Buffer requires ExecutionList execution; ScratchBook is unsupported.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming every popup uses TBox Dialog
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Using an unscanned standard Windows dialog Module for a custom application or JavaScript popup.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Identify the dialog technology. Standard Windows dialogs need no scan; custom dialogs require scanning, and JavaScript dialogs use their documented HTML workflow.

examPitfalls.title: Scanning a confirmation popup instead of using TBox Dialog
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Launching a fresh scan every time a webpage or application shows a new 'Are you sure?' style dialog.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use TBox Dialog without scanning only for supported standard Windows dialogs. The current reference explicitly requires scanning customized dialogs.

examPitfalls.title: Misreading ExplicitName as a wildcard-matching switch
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Renaming item#1 to item* on a scanned JSON Module, but the TestCase still only reads one entry or fails to bind at run time.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: ExplicitName=True enables TestStepValue name editing. Validate the actual Module’s selection logic; that parameter alone does not establish full JSON array traversal.

examPitfalls.title: Hard-coding item#1, item#2, item#3 … for a JSON array
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Building a TestCase directly against a fixed set of indexed ModuleAttributes from the scanned sample file.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Check the runtime count and index selection with empty, one-entry and many-entry arrays. Repetition can use a dynamic count, but looping alone does not guarantee that every entry is read once.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A cleanup step uses TBox Delete File at the start of a run, targeting yesterday's export. On a machine where the export never ran, what is the result?

options.text: The TestStep fails because the file is missing.
The TestStep returns a positive result — Delete File passes even if the file does not exist.
Tosca creates an empty file and then deletes it.

practiceQuiz.hint: This behaviour is what makes it safe as a cleanup step — and dangerous as a check.
practiceQuiz.rationale: TBox Delete File returns a positive result whether or not the file was present. That makes it idempotent and ideal for cleanup, but it means a passing Delete step is never evidence that the file existed — use TBox File Existence for that.

optionExplanations.A: A missing match produces a positive delete result, not this failure.
optionExplanations.B: Positive missing-file deletion is documented; it does not prove the file existed.
optionExplanations.C: The Module executes and reports the missing file rather than this automatic skip.
optionExplanations.D: It does not create a missing file merely to remove it.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A TestCase must copy a report into C:\TestOutput\Archive\, a folder that does not exist yet. What must happen first?

options.text: Nothing — TBox Copy File creates the directory automatically.
A TBox Create Folder step, because Copy File requires the target directory to exist at run time.
The file must be zipped first.
The path must be changed to a network share.

practiceQuiz.hint: Some file Modules create their destination; Copy is not one of them.
practiceQuiz.rationale: TBox Copy File requires the target directory to already exist at run time, as does TBox Move/Rename File. TBox Create Folder is the step that prepares it.

optionExplanations.A: Copy File requires an existing target directory.
optionExplanations.B: Create Folder prepares the destination required by Copy File.
optionExplanations.C: Zipping is not a prerequisite for copying the report.
optionExplanations.D: A network share does not remove the existing-directory prerequisite.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An export file is generated asynchronously and can take up to a minute to appear. How should the TestCase check for it?

options.text: TBox File Existence with the WaitOn ActionMode.
TBox Delete File, then TBox Create Folder.
TBox File Compare against an empty file.
TBox Read/Create File in Verify mode, repeated manually.

practiceQuiz.hint: One of the ActionModes exists specifically for waiting on a condition.
practiceQuiz.rationale: TBox File Existence supports the WaitOn ActionMode alongside negation (!) and wildcards (*). WaitOn makes the TestCase wait for the file to appear instead of performing a single check that may run too early.

optionExplanations.A: WaitOn waits for the file-existence condition within the configured timeout.
optionExplanations.B: Deleting and creating a folder does not wait for the export file.
optionExplanations.C: Content comparison is not the stated asynchronous existence check.
optionExplanations.D: Manual repetition does not use the dedicated existence waiting operation.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which Module both creates files with written content AND verifies or buffers text content from an existing file?
practiceQuiz.hint: The Module's name states both directions.
practiceQuiz.rationale: TBox Read/Create File creates files and writes text, and also verifies or buffers text content from existing files. It supports UTF-8, UTF-16 and ISO-8859-1 encodings with an optional byte order mark setting.

optionExplanations.A: Append writes text but is not the combined read/verify/buffer Module.
optionExplanations.B: File Compare compares two files rather than creating and buffering text.
optionExplanations.C: This Module supports writing, verification, buffering and waiting on file text.
optionExplanations.D: Existence checks the file’s presence, not its text creation and extraction.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How does TBox Image Compare differ from the PDF 1:1 Compare Module covered in the PDF lesson?

options.text: Image Compare is pixel-accurate (exact match), whereas PDF 1:1 Compare passes when similarity exceeds a specified accuracy.
Image Compare supports a similarity threshold; PDF 1:1 Compare requires an exact match.
Image Compare only works on PDF files.

practiceQuiz.hint: One is strict, the other is configurable — and it is not the one you might expect.
practiceQuiz.rationale: TBox Image Compare performs a pixel-accurate verification of BMP, JPG and GIF files — an exact match. PDF 1:1 Compare instead performs a visual comparison that passes when similarity is above the accuracy you specify.

optionExplanations.A: The documented image Module is pixel-accurate; PDF comparison has configured similarity.
optionExplanations.B: This reverses the described comparison behavior.
optionExplanations.C: Pixel comparison and configurable PDF modes are not identical.
optionExplanations.D: Image Compare accepts BMP, JPG and GIF rather than only PDF.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A TestCase needs to steer the MS Excel application itself — opening it and interacting through its own interface, not just its file data. Which Engine does that?
practiceQuiz.hint: The 'UI' in the name is the tell — it drives the visible application.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Excel UI Engine 3.0 steers the MS Excel application itself, through its own interface. Excel Engine 3.0 (without 'UI') instead steers Excel files directly, without driving the application's UI.

optionExplanations.A: The non-UI engine works on workbook content rather than this interface workflow.
optionExplanations.B: The UI engine is intended for steering the Excel application interface.
optionExplanations.C: Database operations do not steer the Excel UI.
optionExplanations.D: HTML Modules serve browser tasks, not Excel application controls.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which Engine steers MS Excel files directly, reading and writing cell data without driving the Excel application's own interface?
practiceQuiz.hint: The one WITHOUT 'UI' in its name works on the file, not the application.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Excel Engine 3.0 steers Excel files directly. Excel UI Engine 3.0 is the one that drives the application's own interface.

optionExplanations.A: This is the Excel application interface workflow.
optionExplanations.B: This engine performs workbook-content operations without visible UI steering.
optionExplanations.C: Database data is a different target than the stated workbook.
optionExplanations.D: Expression evaluation is not workbook manipulation.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which Engine is used to query and steer data sets held in one or more databases?
practiceQuiz.hint: Its name says exactly what it connects to.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Database Engine 3.0 queries and steers data sets across one or more databases.

optionExplanations.A: Workbook operations are not the database SQL connection workflow.
optionExplanations.B: Browser operations do not replace the database engine’s SQL operations.
optionExplanations.C: This engine performs database operations with the supported connection Modules.
optionExplanations.D: Expression verification does not establish a database connection and execute SQL.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Actions like Execute JavaScript, Open a URL, and Close Browser — which group of Modules covers these browser/document-level actions?
practiceQuiz.hint: These act on the browser session itself, not on one control inside the page.
practiceQuiz.rationale: HTML modules cover browser/document-level actions such as Execute JavaScript, Open a URL, and Close Browser — distinct from Modules that steer individual HTML controls.

optionExplanations.A: The HTML group includes these XBrowser operations.
optionExplanations.B: This is Excel interface automation, not browser operations.
optionExplanations.C: This compares expressions rather than executing these browser actions.
optionExplanations.D: This operates on databases, not browser sessions.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which Module compares numeric, string, and alphanumeric expressions?
practiceQuiz.hint: It lives under Expression Evaluation, not under File Operations.
practiceQuiz.rationale: TBox Evaluation Tool (Standard subset → TBox Automation Tools → Expression Evaluation) compares numeric, string, and alphanumeric expressions. TBox File Compare instead compares the content of two files.

optionExplanations.A: This compares file content rather than the stated expression.
optionExplanations.B: The Evaluation Tool verifies expression results as TRUE or FALSE.
optionExplanations.C: Partial Buffer operates on part of a value rather than the expression comparison tool.
optionExplanations.D: Image comparison is unrelated to numeric or string expression evaluation.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which XML Engine Module verifies XML resource content by using DotNet XPath expressions?
practiceQuiz.hint: Its name states the action directly.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Verify XML checks XML resource content using DotNet XPath expressions. Open/Create XML file creates a new file or loads an existing one as a Resource; Create XML Resource makes an empty resource; Save XML file writes the resource's changes back to the connected file.

optionExplanations.A: Save XML writes resource changes, not this XPath content assertion.
optionExplanations.B: Create XML Resource creates an empty resource rather than asserting its content.
optionExplanations.C: Verify XML applies the documented XPath content check.
optionExplanations.D: Open/Create loads or creates a resource/file rather than this assertion.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which Module lets a TestCase open an application or run an executable file?
practiceQuiz.hint: It lives under Process Operations.
practiceQuiz.rationale: TBox Start Program (TBox Automation Tools → Process Operations) opens applications or executable files from a TestCase.

optionExplanations.A: Start Program launches the specified executable or application.
optionExplanations.B: Name To Buffer stores a TestCase name, not launching a process.
optionExplanations.C: Partial Buffer extracts or verifies part of a value.
optionExplanations.D: Clipboard handles Windows clipboard text, not process launch.

practiceQuiz.scenario: During ExecutionList execution, which Module buffers the name of the TestCase that uses it?
practiceQuiz.hint: One Buffer Operations Module names itself after what it captures.
practiceQuiz.rationale: TBox Name To Buffer buffers the name of the TestCase that uses the Module. TBox Set Buffer stores a value you supply yourself, and TBox Partial Buffer extracts or verifies only part of a larger value. This functionality is not supported in ScratchBook.

optionExplanations.A: Set Buffer stores or verifies a supplied value rather than automatically using this TestCase name.
optionExplanations.B: Name To Buffer provides the TestCase name in ExecutionList execution, not ScratchBook.
optionExplanations.C: Partial Buffer handles a portion of a value rather than this automatic name source.
optionExplanations.D: Delete Buffer removes values instead of capturing a name.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which Module verifies or buffers only part of a value, rather than the whole thing?
practiceQuiz.hint: 'Partial' is the giveaway.
practiceQuiz.rationale: TBox Partial Buffer verifies or buffers only part of a value. TBox Set Buffer stores a full value you supply, and TBox Name To Buffer stores the current TestCase's own name.

optionExplanations.A: Set Buffer uses a supplied value, not the partial extraction operation.
optionExplanations.B: Partial Buffer extracts or verifies a specified part of a value.
optionExplanations.C: Name To Buffer captures the TestCase name rather than an arbitrary substring.
optionExplanations.D: Delete Buffer removes buffers instead of extracting a substring.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which Module copies text to the Microsoft Windows clipboard, or verifies/buffers text already on it?
practiceQuiz.hint: It lives under Basic Windows Operations, named after what it touches.
practiceQuiz.rationale: TBox Clipboard copies text to the Windows clipboard, or verifies/buffers text already there.

optionExplanations.A: Clipboard supports writing, verification, buffering and waiting on Windows clipboard text.
optionExplanations.B: Send Keys sends keyboard commands instead of directly accessing clipboard contents.
optionExplanations.C: Start Program launches a process, not clipboard text operations.
optionExplanations.D: Dialog identifies and confirms dialogs, not clipboard contents.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Verifying whether a folder exists, or creating/copying/deleting one — which group of Modules covers this?
practiceQuiz.hint: Distinct from the File Operations folder alongside it.
practiceQuiz.rationale: TBox Create Folder, Copy Folder, Delete Folder, and Folder Existence make up the Folder Operations Modules group — separate from the File Operations folder that handles individual files.

optionExplanations.A: File operations address individual files rather than these folder tasks.
optionExplanations.B: Folder Operations contains creation, copy, deletion and existence Modules.
optionExplanations.C: Buffer operations address values rather than directory operations.
optionExplanations.D: Windows UI operations are distinct from filesystem folder operations.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A custom application dialog is not handled by an unscanned TBox Dialog step. What distinction does the current reference require?

options.text: TBox Dialog cannot click buttons, only read them.
Standard Windows dialogs can be handled without scanning, but customized dialogs must be scanned.
Caption must always be empty for all dialogs.
Every popup is automatically a standard Windows dialog.

practiceQuiz.hint: Separate standard Windows and customized dialogs.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The reference explicitly distinguishes unscanned standard Windows dialogs from customized dialogs that require scanning. Case changes do not replace this technology check.

optionExplanations.A: The Module can confirm standard dialog buttons; it is not read-only.
optionExplanations.B: The reference separates standard Windows dialogs from custom dialogs requiring scan.
optionExplanations.C: Caption identifies the window; universally omitting it is not the solution.
optionExplanations.D: A custom popup is not automatically a standard Windows dialog.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the supported no-scan use case for TBox Dialog?

options.text: Standard Microsoft Windows dialogs identified by Caption, optional Label and Button.
It only works on the Demo Web Shop.
It requires a separate licence per application.
It replaces the need for an Open/Close pattern in every Module family.

practiceQuiz.hint: Nothing about it was produced by scanning a specific popup.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The standard Module can handle Windows dialogs without scanning. This is not a guarantee for arbitrary application or JavaScript popups.

optionExplanations.A: This is the documented standard Windows dialog no-scan scope.
optionExplanations.B: The Module is not restricted to a particular demo webshop.
optionExplanations.C: The stated per-application license rule is not established by the reference.
optionExplanations.D: Dialog handling does not replace other engines’ resource lifecycle steps.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does Configuration Param ExplicitName=True actually enable?

options.text: Automatically traversing every JSON array entry.
Editing the name of the referenced XTestStepValue.
Automatically rescanning the file whenever its length changes.
Switch from the JSON Engine to the XML Engine.

practiceQuiz.hint: The parameter controls name editability.
practiceQuiz.rationale: ExplicitName=True makes the referenced TestStepValue name editable. It is not an automatic wildcard-binding or array traversal switch.

optionExplanations.A: Name editability does not automatically traverse JSON entries.
optionExplanations.B: This is the parameter’s documented function.
optionExplanations.C: The parameter does not automatically trigger rescanning.
optionExplanations.D: It does not change a JSON workflow into an XML engine workflow.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A TestStepFolder should repeat a validated number of times and use the current pass in buffer names. Which mechanisms fit?

options.text: TBox Evaluation Tool and TBox File Compare.
Set Repetition to the validated count or dynamic expression, and use {REPETITION} in the repeated values and buffer names.
TBox Partial Buffer and TBox Clipboard.
Rerunning the same TestCase manually once per entry.

practiceQuiz.hint: One property turns a folder into a loop; one token tracks which pass it's on.
